p.i: stulet, aut reprehendat, quin populus meus sic se habet, ut qui litiget cū sacerdotib. etc. Et ca. 9. Ne læteris Israel ad exultationem ut gentes, quia scortatus es à Deo tuo, & dilexisti mercedem propter omnia horrea fru-menti. Horreum & torcular non pascet eos, & mustum fallet eos. Non habitabunt in terra Domini, sed revertetur Ephraim in Ægyptum, atque in Assyriam, & comedent immundum.

Amos 4.cap. exprobrat populo, quod pe-regrinationes religionis ergò, in Bethel in-stituerint, idololatricis cultibus sese pollue-rint. Idcirco dicit Dominus. Ego vobis dedi munditiem dentium, etc. quem locum nuper citavi. Sensus est. Non opus habebunt den-tifricijs, quibus carnes, quæ dentibus adhæ-sissent, elicerent, vix panem atrum habere poterunt.
Ex his testimonijs sacrarum literarum, sa-tis superq, constat, caritatem & famem pœnam esse scelerum, in primis idololatriæ, & falsi cultus falsorum Deorum.
Atq; hæc quidem in genere, & præsertim

page.notes: The line-end hyphens in "fru-menti", "pollue-rint", "den-tifricijs", "adhæ-sissent" and "sa-tis" are kept as printed. "superq," is read as printed with a comma after the q; the mark may stand for another abbreviation, but the scan is not clear enough to confirm it. The large initial "A" of "Amos" and "Atq;" is set as an ordinary letter. The page is in italic type throughout; the running head is in small capitals.
